articles.body:
Jalen Green doesn't think taking on more of a playmaker role will change his game.

"Same me, just getting guys involved a little more," Green said. "Making the right reads. If I'm making the right read, it's going to help my offensive game, too. It would be an even thing, but I've always been a good playmaker. I can make the right read sometimes. Sometimes, bad results, but I'm trying to find the right read in general. Step in the right direction. It's not that I can't pass the ball. It's just, let's make the better, the right reads."

Green is entering his second season with the Phoenix Suns looking to expand his game by simply being himself and making the correct decision based on how they're being defended.

"He's going to have the ball more," Suns coach Jordan Ott said. "We saw it as the season progressed, he's got more comfortable in our system, his system, but just make the right read. It's not shoot, pass, do, just make the right read."

Phoenix Suns begin training camp ahead of 2026-27 season. See photos

Green, 24, has averaged just 3.3 assists in his five NBA seasons. He managed just 2.8 a game last season, but Green only played 32 games due to a recurring left hamstring injury.

He remained in Phoenix for most of the offseason to return to full strength and work on improving his overall game with playmaking being one aspect of it.

"It's completely voluntary and he chose to live here and stay here and work out in this facility," Ott said. "He could still live here, stay here and work out somewhere else. We proved to him the building was a helpful place for him, but he has to make the commitment. He did. And we felt it (Tuesday). You'll see it when he plays. I think just think the understanding of reps that he was able to take on the floor was a big piece this summer, but the off-court work, what he's able to do in the weight room, just a consistent weight-room approach, will definitely help him."

Green spent time this summer with two-time NBA MVP Steve Nash to work on improving his playmaker skills.

One of league's greatest point guards ever, Nash led the league in assists five times. He's sixth all-time in career assists with 10,335.

Nash, who starred for the Suns during the early 2000s, took on a senior adviser role with the team last season.

"The pacing, just being able to read the game a little bit better," Green said. "Hearing from somebody of that caliber, being able to sit down and actually watch a workout and critique you as you go, that sticks with you. Just being able to hear him, how he breaks the game down, how he sees it, helps a lot."

Green isn't being asked to play like Nash.

The Suns are just looking for him to stay aggressive and read the play that should lead to either a good shot or pass.

"Make the right play, continuously put yourself in a threat position, which, again, we're going to continue to stress the paint," Ott said. "He can get there. And then when the defender comes, make the right play, when the defender doesn't come, go ahead and be aggressive. So just the evolution of his time in the NBA."

This shift could help relieve Devin Booker from shouldering too much of the playmaker duties so he can look to score even more.

Booker paced the Suns in points per game at 26.1 and assists at six a game last season, but he has seen a decline in his shot attempts since the 2021-22 season, when he hoisted a career-high 20.9 shots a game in averaging 26.8 points a game.

2022-23 season – 20.1 FGAs (career-high 27.8 PPG).

"The game is position-less now," Booker said. "I even talked about what the addition of Miles (Bridges), another person that can make plays. I think everybody on the court needs to be able to have those abilities. Frees up everybody. Makes it a free-flow offense. You learn with experience. You learn by being thrown in the fire, being trusted with those responsibilities and we've been seeing it in camp already with them."

articles.title: He nearly won a U.S. Open and is now playing a new kind of competitive golf
articles.summary: John Peterson was a local qualifier who nearly won the U.S.
articles.body:
It was never about invitations to the fanciest clubs, the biggest sponsorships or the nicest cars.

In fact, for a time it seemed he would be remembered most as a side-door entrant: someone who didn't mind gritting his teeth and grinding out par after par against more talented players, despite a gap in raw ability that was evident even to him.

"In a nutshell… I have felt like I have done more with less than most," Peterson told GOLF.com Tuesday from his truck, en route to pick up supplies for his farm in Texas. "I think that's probably what I'm most proud about when I look back on my golf career."

Like everything else, Peterson's pride came the hard way. He was once one of the best collegiate golfers in the world, winning the 2011 NCAA individual title at LSU , only to emerge from his championship glow and find no guaranteed pathway to the PGA Tour. After failing at Q School and nearly going broke chasing Monday qualifiers and mini-tour starts, Peterson became one of the best underdog stories in the game: a local and sectional qualifier who stood over a birdie putt on the 72nd hole of the 2012 U.S. Open at Olympic Club that would have tied the clubhouse lead. (He lagged it to a foot instead, securing a tie for fourth and a spot in the next year's Masters.) Then he shifted into life as one of the Tour's preeminent everymen, making 91 starts over a handful of seasons. And then came another life change, this time as a pro golf retiree. He lingered on the fringes of the game for a while ( and retired twice! ) before settling down on his farm in Texas with his family.

Peterson has built a new life in the years since. He's the father of four kids, the eldest of whom is 8. He's a business owner, running Westoplex Garage, a Fort Worth company that installs automatic gates, overhead doors and epoxy floors. And he's a casual golfer for the first time in his life, logging roughly 20 rounds a year and, eventually, regaining his amateur status.

"I used to play 20 times in a month," Peterson says with a chuckle. "Golf is just a hobby at this point, and really not even that."

Still, parts of the pro experience lingered in his consciousness. Peterson had been a great golfer, but he had never represented the U.S. in a team event. He was left off the 2011 U.S. Walker Cup team after the best season of his life at LSU, and he never got close to wearing the stars and stripes again.

Peterson thought he might live with that "what if?" forever, and that he might never know what it was like to play for the red, white and blue.

Next week, Peterson will be part of an American side competing against the rest of the world in the annual Bridges Cup , an elite mid-amateur, Ryder Cup-style competition held this year at Trump Turnberry in Scotland.

While his playing time has dwindled, Peterson has worked to sharpen his game. This summer, he teed it up in the Jones Cup, the Sunnehanna Amateur and the Southern Amateur. Earlier this year, he also competed as a wild card in Your Golf Tour , the YouTube circuit co-founded by George and Wesley Bryan, which drew millions of views.

"I'd spent… nine years playing pro golf, some of it at the highest level in the world, and never been recognized in an airport," he said. "The week after that thing came out, I got stopped three times in the Atlanta airport."

The buzz has faded a bit in the months since, but the experience reinforced something in Peterson's mind: golf is a game of shared experiences. Next week, when he dons the American uniform for the first time, he'll be reminded of something else. Even when your pro career ends, those experiences remain.

"It's not the same, but I still get to wear the red, white, and blue, which is going to be awesome," Peterson said.

articles.title: Public control of water not enough, Green deputy leader says
articles.summary: Rachel Millward says her party would nationalise water companies to reverse years of “radical underinvestment".
articles.body:
Green Party co-deputy leader Rachel Millward has said her party would nationalise water companies in England and Wales, criticising Prime Minister Andy Burnham's plans to bring them under public control as "vague".

Millward told the BBC the country's water system was an "absolutely unmitigated disaster", arguing there had been "radical underinvestment" over decades.

She said Burnham's plan, which involves removing limits on government ownership of shares in water companies and giving mayors more powers to scrutinise them, did not go far enough.

The Green Party of England and Wales has long called for public ownership of water companies, describing privatisation as a failed experiment.

In its 2024 manifesto, the party estimated that nationalising water companies and the five biggest retail energy firms would cost £30bn over the five years of a parliament.

Last year, the government estimated that nationalising the water industry would cost approximately £100bn.

Millward is expected to make a speech about the party's latest policy on nationalising water companies - and how to pay for it - at the Green Party conference in Brighton this weekend.

It comes as the government considers the option of nationalising Thames Water, which is facing a severe financial crisis.

Ahead of the conference, Millward did a round of interviews with local BBC radio stations across England.

Under the leadership of Zack Polanski, the party's brand of "eco-populism" has posed a challenge to Labour on the left of British politics.

Labour's polling numbers have improved markedly in recent months, suggesting Burnham may be winning back some supporters that had drifted towards Polanski's party.

In her interviews, Millward said the party had had a "historic successful year" by winning a by-election in Gorton and Denton, and making significant gains in May's local elections.

She told BBC Radio Newcastle if it had not been for the rise of the Greens, then Sir Keir Starmer - who was ousted as prime minister by his own MPs - would still be in office.

"We can take the credit for that really," she said.

Millward said Labour's rhetoric had "shifted in our direction" under Burnham.

Going forward she said the Greens would push the Labour government to go further and continue calling for rent controls, nationalisation of water companies and wealth taxes.

But Millward faced some tough questions on local issues, some of which she wasn't able to answer.

She was asked by BBC Radio WM about the bin strikes in Birmingham, where a minority coalition of Liberal Democrats, Greens and independents run the council.

She said she hadn't "been given enough information to answer that question" and apologised several times.

"I'm sorry it's not in my briefing, it should have been," she said. "I'm happy to come on another time and chat about it."

These BBC local radio rounds can be tricky, with presenters often asking about issues in their patches.

Millward seemed most comfortable on national topics, arguing the Greens "have the power to set the agenda for this government" and hold Burnham to account.

The Greens have five MPs and hundreds of councillors across the country.

Green Party leader Zack Polanski is currently contesting the Holborn and St Pancras by-election, which will take place next week. A full list of candidates is available on the BBC website .

articles.title: Jayden Reed sends encouraging message after Packers place him on injured reserve
articles.summary: Jayden Reed is facing a murky recovery after a neck injury abruptly ended his involvement in the Green Bay Packers’ 20-17 overtime win over the New York Jets...
articles.body:
Jayden Reed is facing a murky recovery after a neck injury abruptly ended his involvement in the Green Bay Packers ' 20-17 overtime win over the New York Jets . The wide receiver went down during the second offensive play and was taken away on a backboard before remaining overnight at a hospital in New York.

Reed had agreed to a three year, $50 million extension with Green Bay in April, but the team does not yet know when he will be able to return. James Palmer said on NFL on Prime that there is no established timeline for Reed, with the possibility of a season ending absence still on the table as the Packers proceed with maximum caution.

The 26-year-old's potential absence for the remainder of the season would be a major setback for the Green Bay Packers offense. Adam Schefter later confirmed on X that Green Bay is placing Reed on injured reserve because of his neck injury, leaving him sidelined indefinitely.

Jayden Reed on his injury with the Packers

Despite the difficult circumstances, the Packers star offered an encouraging message to his followers on Instagram, writing, "God will use the unusual to do the unexpected… 11 out."

Reed's positive mindset gives the Green Bay Packers something to hold onto as the team continues dealing with a growing list of injuries. Matt LaFleur said Reed's teammates were encouraged after he regained feeling throughout his body earlier in the week, but the Packers remain committed to taking a careful approach with his recovery.

With Reed unavailable, Skyy Moore and Bo Melton are expected to take on more responsibility in the slot, adding another challenge for an offense already dealing with major problems along the offensive line. Right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele is also out for the season after suffering a patellar tendon tear, leaving Green Bay with even more uncertainty up front.

articles.title: Phil Mickelson Opens Up On His Rehab Stint
articles.summary: Phil Mickelson checked himself into a treatment facility earlier this year as he dealt with “family trauma and addiction,” according to a statement from his...
articles.body:
Phil Mickelson checked himself into a treatment facility earlier this year as he dealt with "family trauma and addiction," according to a statement from his representatives provided to multiple media outlets .

The disclosure adds context for Mickelson's prolonged absence from professional golf during a 2026 season in which the six-time major champion was almost absent from competition.

Mickelson, 56, is no longer at the facility. He played just once on the LIV Golf schedule , appearing at the league's event in South Africa, and missed all four major championships. He had exemptions that would have allowed him to compete in three of them.

His absence initially came with considerably less detail. Mickelson cited a "family health matter" when he stepped away from LIV Golf early in the season. In April, when confirming he would not play in the Masters, he said that he and his family were dealing with a "personal health matter."

More information emerged as the year progressed.

In June, reports indicated that Mickelson had lost his membership at The Farms Golf Club, his longtime club in Rancho Santa Fe, following an allegation that he made inappropriate, non-consensual contact with a female employee. The Farms did not publicly identify Mickelson, but the club confirmed that an incident had taken place and that a member had been removed.

Mickelson's attorney denied the allegations and said that "any misunderstanding has been cleared up." At the time, his attorney again said Mickelson was focused on a family health matter.

Weeks later, Ashley Perez, professional golfer Pat Perez's ex-wife, publicly described several alleged incidents involving Mickelson. Among her accusations was a claim that Mickelson propositioned her for sex in 2015.

After publishing Perez's account, Mickelson's attorney released another statement that offered a clearer indication of what Mickelson had been dealing with privately, saying he was in recovery and had the support of his wife, Amy.

"Recovery is not a straight line," the statement said. "Throughout their 35-year relationship, his wife, Amy Mickelson, has supported Mr. Mickelson and their family with extraordinary grace, unwavering love and the belief that people are measured not only by their failures, but by what they do to make them right."

The statement continued by saying Mickelson's priority was becoming "the husband, father, and man his family deserves," while asking that the family's private health matters remain private.

Mickelson has previously spoken publicly about his struggles with gambling addiction, making addiction a subject he had addressed well before the latest disclosure about his treatment.

A Major-Championship Streak Comes to an End

These developments have unfolded amid a dramatic shift in Mickelson's presence in professional golf. Once one of the sport's most recognizable and consistently discussed players, he has become increasingly limited in his competitive appearances. At the same time, a series of controversies and personal issues have drawn attention away from his play.

The 2026 season represented the most striking example yet. Mickelson failed to appear in any of golf's four majors for the first time since 1989, ending a run that stretched across more than three decades.

Now, a statement from his representatives fills in part of what happened during those months away. What had previously been described publicly as a family or personal health matter included Mickelson entering treatment for family trauma and addiction. At the same time, his golf career was effectively placed on hold.

articles.body:
It's one of 45 tournament's on the PGA Tour in 2026. It's the second of eight FedEx Cup Fall series events.

Welcome to the Bank of Utah Championship , a now three-year-old event in Ivins, Utah, in the southern part of that state.

Black Desert Golf Course provides the stunning landscape for this event. It was the final golf course designed by Tom Weiskopf .

Key number for the Bank of Utah Championship

11. That's how many under the winner has played the par 4s at Black Desert Resort in the previous two editions of this tournament. The two winners at this event have a par-4 birdie or better percentage of 34.09 percent compared to only 21.15 percent by the rest of the field.

Utah's favorite son is making his tournament debut finally. Finau, 37, is a six-time PGA Tour winner and serves as an ambassador of the Korn Ferry Tour event in Utah but he's been unable to play here the past two years. "To have a PGA Tour event in Utah and now to be participating in it on this stage for a home crowd, I'm really excited about it," he said Wednesday. Finau went to West High School in Salt Lake City and won the Utah State Amateur Championship in 2006.

What's the prize money at the 2026 Bank of Utah Championship?

The total purse for the 2026 Bank of Utah Championship is $6 million, the same as it was in 2025. The winner of the 2026 Bank of Utah Championship receives $1.08 million, or 18 percent of the total purse.

Who are the past winners of the Bank of Utah Championship?

In 2024, Matt McCarty posted a final-round 4-under 67 on Sunday and win the inaugural Black Desert Championship in Ivins, Utah, in just his second start on the PGA Tour.

In 2025, Michael Brennan bombed his way around the course to win in just his third PGA Tour start.

Where is the Bank of Utah Championship played?

Black Desert Resort opened in 2023 and quickly rocketed up several of the Golfweek's Best rankings:

T-30 in the top 200 resort golf courses in the U.S.

T-38 in the top 100 public-access golf courses in the U.S.

101 in the top 200 modern golf courses in the U.S.

The golf course plays as a par 71 and measures 7,421 yards for the pros. The property has dramatic lava rock outcroppings all over. The National Park Service reports that the latest volcanic eruption was 32,000 years ago from what is now Snow Canyon State Park, just a couple of miles north of the golf course. The site for Black Desert looks much more like something to be found in Hawaii, minus the ocean views, but with plenty of promise.

Weather forecast for 2026 Bank of Utah Championship

It's going to be warm, if not downright hot, this week and there's virtually no chance of rain in the southern Utah area, according to the weather forecast provided by accuweather .

articles.title: Matthew Golden Left Heartbroken by Tough Packers News
articles.summary: The blows just keep on coming to Matthew Golden and the Green Bay Packers, who are only 1-2 after three weeks of the 2026 NFL season. Even in their lone win...
articles.body:
The blows just keep on coming to Matthew Golden and the Green Bay Packers , who are only 1-2 after three weeks of the 2026 NFL season.

Even in their lone win thus far against the New York Jets in Week 2, the Packers didn't look particularly convincing, and making matters worse was the neck injury suffered by wide receiver Jayden Reed during that contest .

Reed is done for the rest of the season, leaving a significant hole in the team's Jordan Love-led passing attack. Among those counted upon by Green Bay to step up and help cover the void left by Reed is rising wideout Golden, who has led the Packers in receiving yards in each of the last two games.

Matthew Golden Speaks up on Reed After Latter's Season-Ending Neck Injury

Talking to reporters, Golden expressed his thoughts on Reed, who has helped him in more ways than one in adjusting to life in the pros.

"I'm kind of hurt to because me and J Reed got tight. I seen how much work he put in this offseason. The impact he had on me coming into my second year… I feel like we have a good connection," the former Texas Longhorns star wide receiver Golden said on Wednesday, via Vince Lovergine of WLUK-TV FOX 11 .

With Reed out, Golden can be expected to get even more looks downfield. He is coming off a breakout game with 100 receiving yards and a touchdown (his career's first in the regular season) on five catches and 12 targets, albeit in a 35-14 loss to the Atlanta Falcons at Lambeau Field in Week 3.

Golden will look to keep it going in Week 4, as Green Bay aims to get back to its winning ways and avoid a 1-3 record when the team takes on the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on the road this coming Sunday.

Selected by Green Bay in the first round of the 2025 NFL Draft, Golden has 253 receiving yards and a touchdown on 15 receptions through three games this season.

articles.title: Here comes Kevin Zeitler to save the day
articles.summary: One veteran can’t really save the Packers’ entire season on his own, can he?
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers desperately needed help on the offensive line — particularly at guard. There, out on the open market, was veteran Kevin Zeitler , finally healthy after rehabbing a quad injury during the offseason. Packers fans had spent the last few weeks theorizing about the Wisconsin native and former Badger All-American coming in to save the day, at least at one position on the line; thankfully, the Packers recognized the fit and made it happen.

Is Zeitler really a panacea for everything plaguing the Packers' offense? Certainly not. But if he can stabilize one of those interior spots and just not let free rushers through on damn near every play , that will go a long way to helping Jordan Love lead a competent offense.

Meanwhile, you can put to bed any projection of an outside zone running scheme with the recent changes up front. With the line likely to eventually consist of Aaron Banks or Laken Tomlinson at left guard, Zeitler at right guard, and Anthony Belton at tackle, the Packers will almost assuredly be back on board with the power run game. Hopefully that sets up well for a big back like Kaleb Johnson , even if he played in a zone scheme in college.

Zeitler alone won't save the Packers' season. The other players and the coaching staff need to do their part. But it does feel like Zeitler's arrival could be a catalyst that dramatically changes the trajectory of this team's 2026 campaign.

For Packers and Kevin Zeitler, Here's Why It's Dream Fit | SI.com It's not hard to explain: Zeitler is from Waukesha, just outside of Milwaukee. He played at Wisconsin. Now he has a chance to wind down his career in his home state.

New Packers OL Kevin Zeitler already making case to start in Week 4 | Packers Wire It's hard to imagine even a rusty Zeitler playing worse than Jacob Monk has in his three games so far this year.

Meanwhile, Zeitler explains when the Packers contacted him:

Veteran linemen expected to 'settle things down' for Packers up front | Packers.com Between Zeitler and Laken Tomlinson, who took #1 reps at left guard on Wednesday, the team could have a new-look interior line as early as this Sunday.

Green Bay Packers offensive line must give Jordan Love time to be himself | Packersnews.com That line has to do enough to let Love cook, because the Packers still can't rely on the run game right now. But if they can at least keep Love from getting pressured quickly all the time, he's plenty good enough to lead a solid offense.
